claims.text: Adding a small amount of Nb to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Adding a small amount of Nb will preserve the room-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Adding Nb will preserve the high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Nb is an appropriate addition for improving or retaining elevated-temperature strength because it has a high melting point.
The Nb-modified alloy will have a body-centered cubic crystal structure.
Nb addition will produce solid-solution strengthening in HfMoTaTiZr.
Nb addition will refine the grains of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Solid-solution strengthening and grain refinement will maintain the alloy's yield strength.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa under uniaxial compression.
The Nb-modified alloy will retain a yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C under uniaxial compression.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Adding more Nb can increase ductility in the Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy family.
Ti or Zr additions decrease both elevated-temperature strength and density in this alloy family.
Yield strength, density, and microstructure should be measured after Nb addition.
The hypothesis is rejected if room-temperature or 1000 °C yield strength falls by more than 10%, or if density rises by more than 5%, relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires reduced density, but the rejection rule permits unchanged density or a density increase of up to 5% without falsification.
The predicted room-temperature threshold is above 1500 MPa, but a result as low as 1440 MPa would remain within a 10% decrease from the 1600 MPa baseline and would not trigger rejection.
The predicted 1000 °C threshold is above 800 MPa, but the 10% rejection rule would allow strengths down to 769.5 MPa relative to the 855 MPa baseline.
